text:
First Direct, Monzo, and Starling Bank consistently top UK customer service rankings. Which one is "best" for you depends on how you prefer to bank—specifically whether you want to speak to a human on the phone or handle everything seamlessly inside an app.

Independent consumer surveys (such as the Competition and Markets Authority (CMA) service quality survey and Which? customer satisfaction ratings) highlight the top performers across key categories:

Bank	Type	Best For	Standout Service Feature
First Direct	Telephone / Online	Speaking to a human	24/7 UK-based phone support with no automated menus; answers typically within seconds.
Starling Bank	App-only	App reliability & 24/7 chat	Consistently ranks at or near the very top for overall service and online/mobile banking in CMA surveys.
Monzo	App-only	Speed & modern features	Fast in-app chat support, instant notifications, and proactive fraud/spending controls.
Nationwide	High Street	In-person branch access	Highest-rated traditional building society; committed to keeping physical branches open longer than major rivals.
How They Compare

If you want traditional phone support (First Direct): Owned by HSBC, First Direct operates without physical branches (though you can pay in cash/cheques at Post Offices). It has won nearly every major UK customer service award over the last decade because a real person in the UK answers the phone almost immediately, 24/7.

If you want a seamless digital experience (Starling & Monzo): Both are fully licensed UK banks that have disrupted the market by making everyday banking effortless. Starling tends to edge ahead slightly in official CMA overall service quality scores and has zero fees on overseas spending, while Monzo is widely praised for its intuitive app design and budgeting tools.

If you want a physical branch (Nationwide): Traditional high street banks (like Barclays, Lloyds, and NatWest) generally sit in the middle of the pack for customer service. If walking into a branch matters to you, Nationwide Building Society regularly outperforms the major high street banks in customer satisfaction.

(Note: Because you are under 18, your specific account options—such as Monzo Under 16s/16–17, Starling Kite, or Nationwide FlexOne—will have slightly different features than standard adult accounts, though the underlying customer support teams remain the same.)
